headline: Warp Panda's log-blinding VMware bug enters KEV as Cisco and Palo Alto report live attacks
standfirst: CISA's catalog addition for a VMware ESX logging flaw confirms exploitation in a legal-sector espionage case, while Cisco and Palo Alto Networks both report live attacks on edge appliances. Also in today's briefing: a critical Linux kernel TCP bug with an AI-written exploit, a reported federal identity breach, and a large Chrome extension hijack.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

CISA added CVE-2026-41709 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after the VMware ESX flaw was tied to attacks on the U.S. legal sector by the China-nexus actor Warp Panda [[s43]]. On paper it is small: NVD describes insufficient logging (CWE-778) that lets a malicious administrator perform operations without them being recorded, scoring 2.7 LOW with high privileges required and no user interaction. KEV membership, not the score, is the signal. CISA's required action — apply vendor mitigations under its risk-based federal patching directive — binds federal agencies, not everyone, and the supplied text does not describe the post-exploitation chain.

Cisco released patches for CVE-2026-76418, an 8.6 HIGH flaw in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Secure Firewall ASA and FTD software, saying it has been exploited in the wild [[s33]]. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send a crafted request that reloads the device, a denial of service, but the trigger requires secondary authentication configured on a tunnel group, so exposure varies by deployment. It is not in KEV; a catalog miss is not proof of safety.

Palo Alto Networks says active exploitation has been observed against management interfaces exposed to the internet, targeting the recently patched PHP2Shell flaws [[s44]]. No CVE identifiers came with this item, so the vendor advisory is the authoritative list. Analysis: an administrative plane reachable from the internet is the exposure itself; patching narrows it, and the supplied text says nothing about what attackers did afterwards.

## Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-98432, a use-after-free in the Linux kernel's TCP handling, carries a 9.8 CRITICAL rating and affects Ubuntu, RHEL and other distributions [[s6]]. The exploit is the notable part: Anthropic said its AI model wrote one that lets a remote attacker with no credentials run commands as root. The CVE is not in KEV, and the structured record supplies no affected version ranges, so patch status must be checked per distribution rather than inferred. Analysis: the vector — network, no privileges, no user interaction, full confidentiality, integrity and availability impact — is about as bad as kernel bugs get.

## Breaches

More than 41,000 DHS employee records were reportedly leaked after personal and work information was allegedly stolen from an Okta single sign-on system earlier this year [[s22]]. Both the leak and the theft are described as alleged; no confirmation, additional scope or remediation was supplied. Identity providers stay the centre of federal breach risk for the obvious reason: a compromised SSO tenant sits upstream of everything it authenticates.

## Research

319 Chrome extensions with a combined 13.4 million reported installs were hijacking searches, redirecting queries through tracking servers to generate advertising revenue from Bing and Yahoo [[s3]]. No CVE or extension list was supplied. Analysis: install counts describe the internet, not your estate — the operative question is which of these sit in your browser fleet.

Cisco Talos documented NIK C2, a new AI-integrated command-and-control framework observed in the wild [[s36]]. The excerpt offers no victimology, tooling detail or attribution. Analysis: "AI-integrated" is a descriptor, not a capability claim; the practical signal is model assistance folded into unglamorous C2 work rather than anything autonomous.

## Industry

U.S. law enforcement seized the primary domain of Virtualine, a bulletproof hosting service advertised on cybercrime forums for facilitating illegal activity [[s47]]. No operator, charges, or hosting footprint beyond the seized domain were supplied. Analysis: a domain seizure removes a storefront and a brand; the underlying capacity usually reappears under a new name.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period

tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the
child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it.

Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same
request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req().
tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt
under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and
ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice.

Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a
reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop()
calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed.

Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests
into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding
the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being
freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do
not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt
with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in
ip_options_build().

A similar issue exists with request socket migration
(net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE
program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with
inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone
share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the
pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old
request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK,
or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is
freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree().

Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt
(do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use
kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and
tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well.

IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()
duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same
migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This
will be addressed in a separate patch.

selected.angle: A 9.8-rated Linux kernel TCP use-after-free spanning Ubuntu and RHEL now has an AI-written exploit that yields root without credentials, raising urgency for kernel patch cycles.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, formerly SD-WAN vSmart, and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, formerly SD-WAN vManage, contain an authentication bypass vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to bypass authentication and obtain administrative privileges on an affected system. This vulnerability exists because the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted requests to an affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to log in to an affected Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller as an internal, high-privileged, non-root user account. Using this account, the attacker could access NETCONF, which would then allow the attacker to manipulate network configuration for the SD-WAN fabric.
kev.requiredAction: Please adhere to CISA’s guidelines to assess exposure and mitigate risks associated with Cisco SD-WAN devices as outlines in CISA’s Emergency Directive 26-03 (URL listed below in Notes) and CISA’s “Hunt & Hardening Guidance for Cisco SD-WAN Devices (URL listed below in Notes). Adhere to the applicable BOD 22-01 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are not available.

nvd.description:
A vulnerability in the peering authentication in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, formerly SD-WAN vSmart, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, formerly SD-WAN vManage, and Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Validator, formerly SD-WAN vBond, could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to bypass authentication and obtain administrative privileges on an affected system.

This vulnerability exists because the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted requests to an affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to log in to an affected Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller as an internal, high-privileged, non-root user account. Using this account, the attacker could access NETCONF, which would then allow the attacker to manipulate network configuration for the SD-WAN fabric.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: preserve shared-frag marker during coalescing

skb_try_coalesce() can attach paged frags from @from to @to.  If @from
has SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG set, the resulting @to skb can contain the same
externally-owned or page-cache-backed frags, but the shared-frag marker
is currently lost.

That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers.  In
particular, ESP input checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding
whether an uncloned nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data().  If TCP
receive coalescing has moved shared frags into an unmarked skb, ESP can
see skb_has_shared_frag() as false and decrypt in place over page-cache
backed frags.

Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when skb_try_coalesce() transfers paged
frags.  The tailroom copy path does not need the marker because it copies
bytes into @to's linear data rather than transferring frag descriptors.
